name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
method: Plyometric bounding drill; quality and distance matter, no max-clean-rep norms exist. Prescribe by sets/contacts, not a rep ceiling.
check: Bounding is a plyometric drill scored on distance and quality. Clean-rep norms don't exist, so not_max_test is correct. Keep it prescribed by contacts or sets.

name: Bench Jump
method: Box/bench jump is a power drill; the standard metric is height, not max reps. No rep norms found.
check: Box and bench jumps are power drills measured by height. Rep norms don't exist, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Depth Jump
method: Depth jumps are reactive-strength plyometrics, measured by jump height or reactive strength index with low fixed volume. Rep ceilings are not a meaningful test.
check: Depth jumps are measured by jump height or RSI (reactive strength index), with low fixed volume. A max-rep test would push people into fatigued, unsafe reps, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Knee Tuck Jump
sources: Tuck Jump Assessment protocol (JSSM 2017 / World Rugby) <https://passport.world.rugby/conditioning-for-rugby/advanced-conditioning-for-rugby-pre-level-2/functional-screening-and-dynamic-testing/the-tuck-jump-test>
method: The only standard is the Myer Tuck Jump Assessment, which is a 10 s technique screen scored by deviations. It has no published rep norms or cutoffs.
check: The Tuck Jump Assessment source (World Rugby passport, a plausible and relevant URL) is a 10 s technique screen scored on faults, not on rep count. not_max_test is correct.

name: Rocket Jump
method: Explosive vertical jump; judged by height and landing quality. No max-rep norms.
check: A single-effort explosive jump scored on height and landing. No rep norms exist, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Side Standing Long Jump
method: Distance jump. Measured in cm, not reps.
check: Scored as distance, not reps. not_max_test is correct.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop
method: Lateral hop is an agility and landing-control drill. Hop tests in the literature measure distance or time, with no max-clean-rep norms found.
check: Hop tests in the literature use distance or time, such as side-hop counts within a fixed time, not a max clean set. not_max_test is correct.

name: Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
method: Balance and landing-control drill. Quality is binary, so a rep ceiling is not meaningful.
check: A landing and balance control drill. A rep ceiling has no meaning here, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Ski hops
method: Time-based plyometric/cardio drill (lateral hops). No hold-seconds norms exist, and effort is set by interval prescription.
check: A timed interval cardio drill with no hold-seconds norms. not_max_test is correct, and the effort is set by interval prescription.

name: Snap Down
method: Landing-mechanics drill from athletic coaching (stance-snap). It is a technique pattern, not a strength test.
check: A drill for landing mechanics, not a strength or endurance test. not_max_test is correct.

name: Standing Long Jump
method: Standing long jump is a fitness test, but it is scored as distance (cm), not reps.
check: A standard fitness test, but it is scored in cm, not reps. not_max_test is correct.

name: Star Jump
sources: Eat This: jumping jacks fitness test <https://www.eatthis.com/jumping-jacks-fitness-test/> ; HuffPost UK: jumping jacks by age <https://huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/jumping-jack-good-number-by-age_uk_6749907ce4b0918713e2cbae>
method: Searched for star jump and jumping-jack norms. Only popular-press per-minute figures exist (Eat This: intermediate 50-60, advanced 70+ per 60 s; HuffPost/Daily Mail age norms men 25: 60-70). They conflict and measure paced cardio over 60 s, not a max clean single set. Mapping them onto the five tiers would be a guess, so no proposal.
check: The only figures are popular-press jumping-jack counts per 60 s. Eat This and HuffPost UK are real, relevant pages, but they disagree with each other and measure paced cardio, not a max clean set. Declining to map them onto the tiers is defensible. If the app needs a band, it should remain an interval prescription.

name: Ab wheel
sources: Strength Level - Ab Wheel Rollout standards (older snapshot) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout> ; Strength Level - Ab Wheel Rollout (current table) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout/lb> ; FitnessVolt - Ab wheel strength standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout/> ; AOL citing Brewer - ab wheel coaching targets <https://www.aol.com/why-ab-wheel-challenging-effective-130000654.html>
method: Median of three published figures at each tier: Strength Level older snapshot (int 6, adv 14), coaching guidance (beginner 3-6, int 8, adv 12-15), Strength Level/FitnessVolt current community table (int ~20-21, adv 39-44, elite 60). Median at intermediate = 8, advanced = 14. Beginner 4 from coaching midpoint, elite 25 set between coaching ceiling and the inflated community table (judgement, anchored on current band). Novice = round(0.67 x 4) = 3. Source spread is very large; the community calculators likely include partial-range reps.
check: Numbers sit sensibly near the pull-up anchor and the current band 1/5/10/18/25, and they keep order with the easier Hollow Body Rock and harder Dragon Flag (both outside this group). FLAG: the AOL/Brewer coaching URL returns 404, so it may be invented or dead and should not be cited. Without it the beginner tier and the low median rest on the older Strength Level snapshot plus judgement. The community tables (int ~21, adv ~39-44) likely count partial reps. Confidence stays low.

name: Abdominal Draw-In
sources: Marathon Handbook / AthleanX / Livestrong stomach vacuum guidance <https://marathonhandbook.com/stomach-vacuum-exercise/>
method: Coaching guidance compiled for the stomach vacuum (same drawing-in move): beginner 5-10 s, intermediate 10-20 s, advanced 30-60 s. Mapped beginner 10, intermediate 20, advanced 40, elite 60; novice = round(0.67 x 10) = 7. No clinical norms exist; only one source family, so low confidence.
check: Numbers kept, status changed from sourced to derived. The only source is stomach-vacuum guidance, which covers a different drill (breath held on the exhale). The abdominal draw-in is done while breathing normally, so these are borrowed values, not a citation. A max hold of a draw-in may not be a meaningful test.

name: Bear plank hold
method: Searched PubMed-style plank norms, strengthlevel, BoxRox, Healthline and others. No hold-time norms for the bear plank exist; only a Healthline note that 3 x 60 s means it is time to progress. Kept the chain: High plank hold (45/65/125/200/325, itself forearm plank x1.2) x1.2 for the easier variant, ceil to 5 s. Elite 390 s is beyond a useful test length; consider capping at 300 s in the app.
check: No norms exist. My extra search for hold norms found only forearm-plank data (Chase et al., CDC, topendsports). The band is High plank x1.2 under the easierId chain, it strictly increases, and it is above High plank at every tier. Elite 390 s is a very long test; capping at 300 s in the app is a product decision.

name: Cat Plank
sources: Fitness norms for the plank exercise (Chase et al.) <https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/ijesab/vol8/iss2/14>
method: No published numbers for this exact hold. Catalogue harderId is Forearm Plank, so Cat Plank is easier: forearm plank anchor 37/55/105/165/270 x1.2 ceil, rounded to 5 s.
check: harderId is Forearm Plank, so this is the easier variant: forearm anchor x1.2 (ceil, 5 s steps). The band strictly increases and is above the forearm anchor 37/55/105/165/270 at every tier. Chase et al. is a sanity check only, not a source for this move.

name: Dynamic side plank
method: No rep norms found. Parent is the Side Plank (easierId hf_100), anchor 15/30/60/90/120 s, converted at about 3 s per controlled hip dip: 5/10/20/30/40. Anecdotal coaching guidance of 10-20 reps per set is consistent with the intermediate value but is not a norm.
check: Parent is Side Plank (hf_100, 15/30/60/90/120 s) at about 3 s per hip dip. The band strictly increases and is plausible next to the crunch and side plank anchors. Only anecdotal coaching guidance of 10-20 reps per set exists, and it fits the intermediate tier.

name: High plank hold
sources: Fitness norms for the plank exercise (Chase et al.) <https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/ijesab/vol8/iss2/14>
method: No straight-arm plank norms found; searches returned only forearm plank data. Forearm plank anchor 37/55/105/165/270 s x1.2 (shorter lever, easier variant) ceil to 5 s.
check: My extra search found no straight-arm plank norms; every result was forearm-plank data. The band is forearm anchor x1.2 and strictly increases. Bear plank (its easierId) is higher at every tier. Its harder variant, plank up-down, counts reps, so the two cannot be compared tier by tier.

name: Incline Plank With Alternate Floor Touch
method: No published numbers. easierId is Forearm Plank (hf_99), so this move is the harder variant of the hold, not an easier one as the first pass assumed. Dynamic plank base (forearm anchor / 4 s per rep = 9/14/26/41/68) divided by 1.2, ceil.
check: The researcher was right to flip the variant direction: easierId is Forearm Plank, so this is the harder variant, dynamic plank base 9/14/26/41/68 /1.2 ceil. The band strictly increases. The 4 s per rep conversion is an assumption. No norms found.

name: Lateral plank walk
method: No published numbers. Same chain as the incline touch: easierId is Forearm Plank, so this is harder. Dynamic plank base 9/14/26/41/68 divided by 1.2, ceil.
check: Same chain and catalogue links as wger_312 (easierId Forearm Plank, harderId hf_125), so the harder rule /1.2 is applied consistently. The band strictly increases. No norms found.

name: Leg Wheel
method: No published numbers. Parent is easierId Plank with Alternating Leg Lift (9/14/26/41/68), so Leg Wheel is the harder variant: parent / 1.2, ceil.
check: Parent is easierId wger_1410 (9/14/26/41/68), and /1.2 ceil gives this band, which strictly increases. The parent is not in this group, so there is no ordering conflict. No norms found for supine leg circles.

name: Plank Jump-In
method: No norms found for plank jump-ins or plank jacks; only anecdotes (one article cites 36 reps in a minute for a different variation). Kept the dynamic plank base from the forearm anchor at 4 s per rep.
check: My extra search found no plank-jack or jump-in norms. The nearest are informal 60-second jumping-jack scales (about 40 below average, 80+ excellent), which are not comparable. The dynamic plank base strictly increases. Its easierId, bear plank, is a hold, so units differ and no ordering check applies. True max reps are likely higher because the move is plyometric, so the band may be conservative.

name: Plank Reach
method: Kept dynamic plank base (forearm plank anchor / 4 s per rep). Searches found no rep or hold norms for this move, only forward-plank norms (Chase et al. 2014 collegiate quartiles 73.5/95/122.5 s women, 84/110/135 s men), which do not give reps for a reach variant.
check: Nothing was marked sourced, so there was nothing to fetch. Five more searches (up-down/commando rep tests, supine plank norms, TRX rollout norms, Strength Level) found only forward-plank hold norms (Chase/Linfield quartiles, Strand et al. 2014) and coaching prescriptions, with no rep norms for plank reach. The dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep) is kept. The band strictly increases and novice >= 1. easierId hf_99 and harderId hf_125 are not in this group.

name: Plank up-down
method: Kept dynamic plank base 9/14/26/41/68 with harder-variant /1.2 (rounded) for the elbow-to-hand transitions. No max-rep norms found for plank up-downs.
check: No rep norms exist. Searches for up-down or commando rep tests returned only plank holds, the Army plank and Fitbod prescriptions of 7-10 reps. The base /1.2 gives 8/12/22/34/57, but advanced 34 and elite 57 are above the push-up anchor (29/36). An up-down rep is a one-arm-led press from elbow to hand, so pressing endurance limits it, not plank endurance. I capped advanced and elite at the push-up anchor (29, 36) and kept novice, beginner and intermediate from base /1.2. The band strictly increases. Neither neighbour (ntc_high_plank, hf_125) is in this group.

name: Plank with Alternating Leg Lift
method: Kept dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep). Searches returned only static plank norms, and the leg-lift search was rate-limited.
check: No leg-lift plank rep norms were found, only forward-plank holds. The dynamic plank base is kept. The band strictly increases. The ordering against harderId wger_1909 (8/12/22/34/57, outside this group) holds per the first pass.

name: Plank-to-Elbow Extension
method: Same family as plank up-down, so dynamic plank base /1.2. No norms found for this move.
check: Same family as plank up-down and same finding: no norms found. Pressing from elbow to hand limits it, so advanced and elite are capped at the push-up anchor (29/36) instead of 34/57, which keeps it equal to plank up-down. The band strictly increases. Neither neighbour (hf_99, hf_125) is in this group.

name: Reverse Plank
method: No reverse plank norms found. The search returned only forward plank data (Chase et al. 2014 collegiate quartiles), so I kept the forearm plank anchor 37/55/105/165/270 as the closest parent. The first-pass band of 35/55/105/165/270 is kept as given.
check: Searches for supine or reverse plank norms found none, only prone forearm plank (Linfield median about 95 s for women and 110 s for men, consistent with the anchor) and one single-leg bridge study (mean 65 s), which is not comparable. The forearm plank proxy is kept, with novice rounded to 35. The band strictly increases. Easier bear plank (outside this group) is higher at every tier.

name: Scissor Kick
sources: FitnessVolt - Flutter kicks strength standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/flutter-kicks> ; Healthline - scissor kicks <https://www.healthline.com/health/scissor-kicks>
method: Single published modelled table (FitnessVolt flutter kicks, 180 lb male: novice 14, intermediate 67, advanced 140, elite 228), mapped novice -> beginner. Time window and counting method unstated (per leg vs per cycle can differ 2x); Healthline's 12-20 reps is a training dose, not a max. Only one numeric source, so low confidence and values are likely high versus the current band.
check: Spot-check of the FitnessVolt page confirms the 180 lb male figures (novice 14, int 67, adv 140, elite 228). It is a modelled estimate and does not say whether each leg counts as a rep. It is the only numeric source, and its 14 -> 67 step (4.8x) and elite 228 are implausible for one clean set. Healthline gives a training dose, not a max. Treated FitnessVolt intermediate 67 as the anchor value and placed the other tiers with hollow-hold ratios (10/20/45/60/90 relative to 45): 15/30/67/89/134.

name: Stomach Vacuum
sources: Marathon Handbook - stomach vacuum exercise <https://marathonhandbook.com/stomach-vacuum-exercise/>
method: Coaching guidance across several articles: beginner 5-10 s, intermediate 10-20 s, advanced 30-60 s. Mapped beginner 10, intermediate 20, advanced 40, elite 60; novice = round(0.67 x 10) = 7. No clinical norms.
check: Coaching guidance (beginner 5-10 s, intermediate 10-20 s, advanced 30-60 s) is mapped sensibly. The hold is limited by breath-holding, which is consistent with a short ceiling. It has only one source family, so confidence stays low.

name: Swimmers
sources: Strength Level - Superman standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/superman>
method: The search found only coaching prescriptions (e.g. 10 reps, 3 rounds of 20), not max-rep norms. Kept the Superman proxy from Strength Level (novice 8, intermediate 25-28, advanced 46-53, elite 81).
check: A search confirmed the Superman proxy on Strength Level: men novice 8, intermediate 28, advanced 53, elite 81, with an older snapshot giving 25/46. The averaged mapping 8/27/50/81 and novice round(0.67 x 8) = 5 are consistent with it. No swimmers-specific norms were found. The jump from beginner 8 to intermediate 27 is steep but comes from the source distribution. The easier variant hf_117 is measured in seconds, so the units cannot be compared.

name: TRX roll out
method: Kept ab wheel (3/4/8/14/25) with the easier-variant rule x1.2 ceil, since the TRX angle is adjustable. The TRX search was rate-limited and no norms were found.
check: Searches for TRX rollout or body-saw norms found only prescriptions (TRX 40/40 body saw at 5-10 reps). The Fitbod standards page returned 403. Ab wheel x1.2 ceil, for the adjustable angle, is kept. The band strictly increases. Neither neighbour (hf_103, hf_108) is in this group.

name: 3/4 Sit-Up
sources: Sit-Ups (1-Min, Cooper): Males, Age 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29> ; StrengthLevel Sit Ups standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/sit-ups/lb> ; StrengthLevel Crunches standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches/lb>
method: Sit-up standards: median per tier of Cooper-labelled 1-min sit-up percentiles (men 20-29), StrengthLevel sit-ups (men), and StrengthLevel crunches (third source because sit-up sources differ 33% at intermediate). Percentile mapping: 20th=beginner, 50th=intermediate, 80th=advanced, 95th=elite. Applied to the 3/4 sit-up as the same family; novice = round(0.67 x beginner).
check: Variant order inverted: easierId hf_115 (Bicycle Crunch 8/12/40/75/120) must sit above at every tier, but the researcher's values were higher at novice, beginner and intermediate, and equal at advanced. Fixed with the harder-variant rule, bicycle / 1.2 (rounded). The sources are full sit-up norms (a 1-minute Cooper test and StrengthLevel sit-ups), not 3/4 sit-up norms, so this is effectively derived. Cooper URL spot-checked and the numbers match.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
sources: StrengthLevel Ab Wheel Rollout <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout> ; FitnessVolt Ab Wheel Rollout standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout/> ; AOL / Brewer coaching guidance on ab wheel <https://www.aol.com/why-ab-wheel-challenging-effective-130000654.html>
method: Community calculators (StrengthLevel, FitnessVolt) give about 5/21/41/65 but differ greatly from coaching guidance (Brewer: 3-6 beginner, ~8 intermediate, 12-15 advanced; FitnessVolt readiness rule 10 kneeling reps; mastery 12-15). Took the median of calculator, Brewer coaching and readiness figures per tier: beginner 5, intermediate 10, advanced 14. Elite extrapolated using the StrengthLevel elite/advanced ratio (about 1.6), giving 22. Novice = round(0.67 x 5).
check: Numbers kept: they sit plausibly near the pull-up anchor 3/4/8/13/18 for an advanced move. The AOL/Brewer coaching URL returned 404 on spot-check, so it is unverified and must be replaced or dropped. Confidence lowered to low, because only the calculators (StrengthLevel and FitnessVolt, about 5/20/40/62, likely kneeling) are verifiable and they are much higher.

name: Abdominal Crunch
sources: StrengthLevel Crunches <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches/lb> ; Cooper 1-min sit-ups men 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29>
method: Average per tier of StrengthLevel crunches (men; novice=20th) and Cooper-labelled 1-min sit-up percentiles (men 20-29) as the nearest published crunch-type test. Intermediate 41 vs 40 (2.5% spread). Avg beginner 23.5, advanced 61, elite 85.5, rounded; novice = round(0.67 x 24).
check: Two sources agree at intermediate (41 vs 40). Tiers increase and the curve is plausible. The Cooper source is a 1-minute sit-up test used as a proxy; noted.

name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
method: Loaded, technique-limited kettlebell lift; max reps depends on bell weight and is not a meaningful bodyweight max test.
check: Load-dependent kettlebell lift, not a bodyweight max test.

name: Air Bike
sources: Strength Level bicycle crunch standards (male) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/bicycle-crunch/kg>
method: Air bike = bicycle crunch; kept parent Bicycle Crunch (hf_115) standard x1.0. Cross-check: Strength Level bicycle crunch male intermediate 39 vs 40 here, agrees. Only one extra community source, so not promoted to sourced.
check: No result in this group was marked sourced, so no downgrades were needed. I opened the Strength Level bicycle crunch page and it shows male Novice 14, Intermediate 39, Advanced 71, Elite 110; the researcher wrote 70/105, so the top two figures have drifted slightly but intermediate 39 still matches. Keeping the Bicycle Crunch (hf_115) band x1.0 is right: air bike is the same movement. The band rises strictly. Only one community source, so it stays derived.

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
method: No published norms found (search for 1-minute heel-touch norms hit a rate limit and returned nothing). Kept parent crunch 16/24/40/60/85 x1.2 (short-range easier move).
check: A web search for heel-touch rep norms found only balance tests, and Strength Level has no heel-touch page. Crunch x1.2 suits a shorter-range, easier move and the band rises strictly. Its harderId (fedb_toe_touchers) is not in this group.

name: Arch Body Hold
sources: Biering-Sorensen young adult men (secondary summary) <https://orthofixar.com/?p=7871> ; Isometric back extensor endurance, Nigerian young adults <https://e-space.mmu.ac.uk/630030/1/Kuwait%20article.pdf> ; Normative study 561 adults 19-67 (via Physio-pedia/MMU) <https://www.physio-pedia.com/Biering-Sorenson_Test>
method: Closest published test is the Biering-Sorensen back-extensor hold (arms/legs not lifted, so only a proxy). Converted mean+SD to percentiles (20th = mean-0.84SD, 80th = +0.84SD, 95th = +1.65SD) for three samples: young men 146+/-51 s, Nigerian young adults 98+/-44 s, mixed adults 113+/-46 s. Spread at intermediate was 42%, so used the median per tier, rounded to 5 s; novice = round(0.67 x 75).
check: Status changed from sourced to derived (proxy): all sources measure the Biering-Sorensen bench hold, not a floor arch/superman hold. Numbers kept. They sit near the forearm plank anchor (37/55/105/165/270) and above the hollow hold (10/20/45/60/90), which fits the arch hold being the easier counterpart. Confidence low.

name: Bent Press
method: Loaded, highly technical kettlebell/barbell lift; rep max depends on external load, not a bodyweight max test.
check: Load-dependent technical lift, not a max test.

name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
sources: Strength Level reverse crunches (male) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/reverse-crunches> ; Strength Level crunches (male) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches/kg>
method: Better parent found: floor reverse crunch. Strength Level reverse crunch male 13/32/55/82 vs its crunch 22/50/85/126 gives ratio ~0.64 to 0.65 per tier. Applied to Aurora crunch 16/24/40/60/85: beginner 15, intermediate 26, advanced 39, elite 55, novice round(0.67x15)=10. Single community source (FitnessVolt table is modelled from Strength Level, not independent), so stays derived.
check: Both Strength Level pages were fetched and confirm the figures: reverse crunches male 13/32/55/82 and crunches male 22/50/85/126. The arithmetic holds: 24x0.64=15, 40x0.64=26, 60x0.65=39, 85x0.65=55, novice round(0.67x15)=10. A floor reverse crunch is a better parent than the hanging knee raise (3/8/12/15/20), and this band sits above that anchor, which is plausible for a floor move. It is still built on a ratio from one community dataset, so it stays derived.

name: Bent-knee Iron Cross
method: Lying knee-drop spinal twist is a mobility/stretch drill, not a meaningful max-reps test.
check: Mobility twist drill, not a max test.

name: Bicycle Crunch
sources: StrengthLevel Bicycle Crunch <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/bicycle-crunch> ; FitnessVolt Bicycle Crunch <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/bicycle-crunch>
method: Two calculators agree at intermediate (StrengthLevel 39, FitnessVolt 42; about 8% spread). Averaged intermediate 40; advanced averaged 71/84 = 78, trimmed to 75; beginner from FitnessVolt novice 10 plus StrengthLevel crunch ratio (14/41) giving 12; elite from FitnessVolt 132 and StrengthLevel ratio (116/41 x 40 = 113) giving about 120. Novice = round(0.67 x 12). Counts are total reps (both sides).
check: StrengthLevel spot-checked: Novice 14, Intermediate 39, Advanced 71, Elite 110 (the researcher omitted the novice and elite figures). Two-source averages: beginner (14+10)/2 = 12, intermediate 40.5, advanced 77.5, elite 121. These match the proposal. Kept as the parent of the sit-up family.

method: Motor-control and stability drill (typically 8-12 slow reps per side); no norms found and max clean reps is not meaningful.
check: Motor-control drill; max reps not meaningful.

name: Black Widow Knee Slides
method: No norms found. Slider knee tuck from plank kept at hanging knee raise anchor x1.0.
check: No norms exist for this move. The hanging knee raise anchor x1.0 is plausible for a slider knee tuck from plank, and the band rises strictly.

name: Body Saw

check: Searches found no Strength Level or other norms for the body saw. Copying Ab Wheel Rollout x1.0 is plausible, since both share the same easier and harder links. Neither hf_103 nor hf_108 is in this group, and the band rises strictly.

name: Bottoms Up
sources: Strength Level reverse crunches (male) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/reverse-crunches>
method: Same lying hip-lift family; re-parented to floor reverse crunch via Strength Level ratio (see bent-knee hip raise).
check: Same lying hip-lift family as the Bent-Knee Hip Raise. The reverse crunch source was fetched and matches (male int 32). This is consistent with the hip-raise re-parenting and the band rises strictly.

name: Butt-Ups
sources: Strength Level reverse crunches (male) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/reverse-crunches>
method: Same hip-lift family; re-parented to floor reverse crunch via Strength Level ratio (see bent-knee hip raise).
check: Same hip-lift family as the Bent-Knee Hip Raise. The reverse crunch source was fetched and matches. Consistent with its siblings, and the band rises strictly.

name: Butterfly Sit Up
method: No direct norms found. Kept first-pass parent (adjusted 3/4 sit-up / 1.2), which already respects the easierId bicycle ordering.
check: No direct norms were found. Its easierId is hf_115 (Bicycle Crunch, 8/12/40/75/120, the same band as Air Bike in this group), and this band is at or below it at every tier (6<=8, 8<=12, 28<=40, 53<=75, 83<=120), so the order is correct. The harderId (jackknife sit-up) is not in this group. The band rises strictly.

name: Cocoons
method: No norms found. Crunch with knee tuck, parent crunch / 1.2.
check: Crunch /1.2 (13.3/20/33.3/50/70.8) is applied correctly to a harder crunch-plus-knee-tuck. The band rises strictly and is plausible.

name: Crab toe touch
method: No norms found. Crunch-level reach move copied from crunch standard.
check: No norms were found. Copying the crunch anchor is plausible for a crunch-level reach move, and the band rises strictly.

name: Cross-Body Crunch
method: No norms found. Rotated crunch at equal difficulty, copied from crunch standard.
check: A rotated crunch at the same difficulty, so the crunch anchor is copied. Its harderId (fedb_sit_up) is not in this group. The band rises strictly.

name: Cross-body mountain climber
sources: Strength Level mountain climbers (male) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/mountain-climbers/kg>
method: Published mountain climber numbers are rep counts of unstated time window (Strength Level male 18/47/85/131), not seconds, so they cannot replace a hold-seconds band. Kept forearm plank / 1.2 rounded to 5 s.
check: The Strength Level mountain climbers page was fetched and confirms male 18/47/85/131 reps. It gives no time window per set (only the dates its data covers), so the figures cannot convert to a hold in seconds and stay reference only. Forearm plank /1.2, rounded to 5 s, is applied correctly. The easierId (hf_121) is not in this group. The band rises strictly.

name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
sources: Strength Level - Decline Crunch <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/decline-crunch> ; Strength Level - Crunches <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches>

name: Elbow to Knee
sources: Strength Level - Bicycle Crunch <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/bicycle-crunch> ; Strength Level - Crunches <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches>
method: The move is a lying cross-body (oblique) crunch with one leg crossed over the other knee, so the bicycle crunch is a closer parent than the 1-minute sit-up norm. Took Strength Level bicycle crunch / crunches ratios per tier (14/22=0.64, 39/50=0.78, 71/85=0.84, 110/126=0.87) and applied them to the crunch anchor 24/40/60/85: 15/31/50/74. Novice = round(0.67 x 15) = 10.
check: Proxy ratios confirmed on Strength Level: bicycle crunch 14/39/71/110 vs crunches 22/50/85/126. Applied to the crunch anchor, the arithmetic checks out: 24x0.64=15, 40x0.78=31, 60x0.84=50, 85x0.87=74, novice round(0.67x15)=10. Strictly increasing, and sensibly below the crunch anchor. This is a better parent than the first-pass 1-minute sit-up norm.

check: Sits at the HKR anchor level, mid-ladder. Its easier (hf_122) and harder (hf_111) moves are outside this group. No data. Strictly increasing.

Still above jackknife sit-up 15/23/28/33/38. Strength Level sit-ups (25/54/90/133) are about 35% above the norm at intermediate, so not combined.
check: Correctly applied the harder-variant /1.2 rule to the sit-up norm (33/40/47/55): 28/34/40/46, with novice 19. Still strictly above harderId jackknife sit-up (15/23/28/33/38). Strictly increasing.

check: Ambiguous move placed on the sit-up norm, consistent with its sit-up easier and harder links. Above harderId jackknife sit-up. Strictly increasing.

anchorMisfire: Confirmed. hf_49 L-Sit Pull-Up carries the plain Endura pull-up band 3/4/8/13/18, matched by name. An L-sit pull-up, which holds hip flexion for the whole rep, is clearly harder than a strict pull-up and should be about pull-up/1.2 = 2/3/6/10/15. The gorilla chin (a pull-up plus a knee tuck) is easier than an L-sit pull-up, and 2/3/7/11/15 sits at or above that corrected band at every tier.

name: Hanging Leg Raise

Status: derived (sources kept as context).

method: Three secondary sources for men. StrengthLevel (community lifts): novice 18, average 47, elite 131. FitnessVolt model (180 lb man): 14/40/71/107. check: Three secondary sources: StrengthLevel 18/47/131, FitnessVolt 14/40/71/107 and Eat This <50/50-70/70-90/90+. name: Oblique Crunches
sources: Strength Level - Side Crunch standards (men) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/oblique-crunch>
method: One real source for a true synonym: Strength Level Side Crunch male table (community data) beginner<1/novice 12/intermediate 33/advanced 58/elite 88. FitnessVolt's Side Crunch table (46 intermediate) comes from the same model, so it is not independent and not averaged in. Mapping: Aurora beginner=12, intermediate=33, advanced=58, elite=88, novice=round(0.67x12)=8. Replaces the sit-up x1.2 derivation, which was a 1-minute test with a narrow spread.
check: Fetched strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/oblique-crunch. It is the Side Crunch page and confirms 12/33/58/88 with a 33-rep average. That is one source, so the item stays derived. The same site's crunches page gives 22/50/85/126, which runs about 1.4 to 1.5 times Aurora's calibrated crunch anchor (16/24/40/60/85). Taking the raw Strength Level numbers would put oblique crunches above the crunch anchor at intermediate and elite, which is implausible. I rescaled each tier by Aurora crunch over Strength Level crunch (1.09, 0.80, 0.71, 0.67): beginner 12x1.09=13, intermediate 33x0.8=26, advanced 58x0.71=41, elite 88x0.67=59, novice round(0.67x13)=9. Bands strictly increase. Caveat: its listed harderId fedb_sit_up (23/34/40/46/55, a 1-minute protocol) is outside this group and sits above this band at beginner and intermediate. The sit-up band is the outlier, since it is also higher than the crunch anchor at those tiers. Count reps as a total.

name: Russian Twist
sources: StrengthLevel Russian twist <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/russian-twist> ; FitnessVolt Russian twist standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/russian-twist>
method: StrengthLevel (9,585 results, men) novice 17, intermediate 42, advanced 72, elite 107, with the novice figure treated as beginner. FitnessVolt (editorial, 180 lb man) 14/41/75/113, mapped the same way. Average per tier, novice = round(0.67 x 16).
check: StrengthLevel (17/42/72/107) and FitnessVolt (14/41/75/113) agree within about 2% at intermediate. The novice-to-beginner mapping and the averaging are correct. FitnessVolt is an editorial model, so the two sources are only partly independent. Confidence is medium.

name: Seated Corkscrew
sources: Strength Level Russian Twist (parent only) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/russian-twist>
method: No corkscrew norms. Parent is Russian twist. Strength Level male Russian twist: Novice 17 / Int 41 / Adv 72 / Elite 108. Keep the first-pass proposal, which agrees with this parent.
check: Fetched the Strength Level Russian Twist page. It says the average male does 41 reps, and the 160 to 180 lb rows (15-17 / 38-42 / 65-71 / 95-104) are consistent with the parent figures quoted. That is a parent-only source. The seated corkscrew inherits the Russian twist band unchanged. This is plausible if twists are counted per touch. Bands strictly increase, and there are no in-group variant neighbours.

name: Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
method: No direct norms. Easier than the hanging knee raise anchor 3/8/12/15/20, so x1.2, ceil. Strength Level's Hanging Knee Raise (9/20/34/50) is much higher but community-skewed, so the calibrated anchor stays the parent.
check: Hanging knee raise anchor x1.2 ceil (3/8/12/15/20 gives 4/10/15/18/24) is correct. It is at or above the harder variant at every tier, and bands strictly increase. Possibly conservative for a supported move, but it follows the variant rule.

name: Seated Knee Tuck
method: Same as Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In: hanging knee raise anchor x1.2, ceil.
check: Same as the seated flat bench leg pull-in: hanging knee raise x1.2 ceil. Correct and strictly increasing, and it sits above the harder variant hanging_knee_raise.

name: Seated Leg Tucks
method: No numeric source found for this move; searches rate-limited. Kept parent hanging knee raise anchor 3/8/12/15/20 x1.2 ceil (seated tuck is easier than hanging).
check: Hanging knee raise anchor 3/8/12/15/20 x1.2 ceil = 4/10/15/18/24; the arithmetic checks. The band matches its sibling Seated Knee Tuck (wger_1105), strictly increases and sits above its harder variant. A StrengthLevel page for this move exists but lists no numbers.

name: Side Crunch
sources: Sit-Ups (1-Min, Cooper) men 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29>
method: No source for this move. Kept sit-up x1.2 ceil from first pass; crunch anchor (16/24/40/60/85) considered as alternative but sit-up is the graph neighbour.
check: The proposed 28/41/48/56/66 used a stale sit-up base (23/34/40/46/55). The current sit-up final is 22/33/40/47/55, and x1.2 ceil of that gives 27/40/48/57/66, the same as Standing Side Crunches. More research found two calculator pages. StrengthLevel side crunch (male) gives <1/12/33/58/88. FitnessVolt (180 lb male) gives 3/21/46/76/110 and calls itself an editorial table, not a measured population. Averaged, they give intermediate about 40, advanced 67 and elite 99, so the derived band is the right order of magnitude. I did not upgrade it to sourced, for three reasons. The calculator scale conflicts with the sit-up chain (StrengthLevel sit-ups are 5/25/54/90/133, which puts the side crunch below the sit-up, the reverse of the graph). Its low tiers (11/17) would fall below the harder sit-up. FitnessVolt is editorial.

name: Side Jackknife
sources: Sit-Ups (1-Min, Cooper) men 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29>
method: No source found. Sit-up / 1.2 rounded, as harder than its easier variant sit-up.
check: The proposed 19/28/33/38/46 came from the stale sit-up base. The current sit-up final 22/33/40/47/55 divided by 1.2 and rounded gives 18/28/33/39/46. It stays below the easier sit-up and above the harder Hanging Leg Raise (hf_110, 2/6/10/12/16). StrengthLevel has no data for this move.

name: Side Plank
method: Kept at calibrated McGill anchor. Found only partial literature: an IJSPT article (ijspt.scholasticahq.com/article/154592) cites a side plank range of 72-94 s, male runners 83.2 s right and 81.5 s left, and general adult males 34 s. Sources disagree widely (34 vs about 83 s) and are not matched populations, so anchor 60 s intermediate retained as a midpoint.
check: The proposed 10/15/30/60/90 contradicted the researcher's own note to keep the anchor, so I restored the calibrated side plank anchor 15/30/60/90/120. More research, as cross-checks only: StrengthLevel side plank (male, all bodyweights) gives 6/24/44/69/95 s, with an average of 44 s. Young healthy adults in McGill-protocol studies average about 81-88 s right and 85-92 s left, as secondary citations report them. The anchor's intermediate of 60 s sits between the general-population calculator (44 s) and the young-adult lab means (about 85 s), so it is plausible. I left it as the anchor and did not re-source it.

name: Side plank hip lifts
method: No source found. Sit-up / 1.2 from first pass; cross-check with side plank anchor (about 2 s per rep within 60 s hold gives about 30 reps).
check: The sit-up/1.2 band (novice 18) is implausible against the side plank anchor. A novice holds a side plank for 15 s, but 18 hip lifts at about 2 s each need about 36 s under a harder, dynamic load. At about 2 s per rep the anchor gives about 8/15/30/45/60, and since the dynamic move is harder, /1.2 brings that to about 6/13/25/38/50. I aligned it with Dynamic side plank (wger_1288, 5/10/20/30/40), which is the same hip-dip movement. Reps are per side. I found no numeric standard: StrengthLevel has no data, Fitbod blocked access, and other pages only give prescriptions of 5-10 per side.

name: Side Plank with Rotation
method: No source found. Sit-up / 1.2 from first pass.
check: The sit-up/1.2 band (18/28/33/39/46) is too high for a side plank variant, for the same reason as the side plank hip lifts. The rotation (thread-the-needle) is harder than a plain hip lift, so I took 5/10/20/30/40 / 1.2 and rounded to get 4/8/17/25/33. Reps are per side. No source found. Its easier move, the side plank, is a hold, so the two cannot be compared tier by tier.

name: Sit Up Elbow Thrust
method: No source found. Sit-up / 1.2 as a harder dynamic sit-up variant.
check: Sit-up 22/33/40/47/55 divided by 1.2 = 18/28/33/39/46; the arithmetic checks. It sits above the harder Jackknife Sit-Up (15/23/28/33/38). Outside this group, its easier move, Bicycle Crunch (8/12/40/75/120), is below it at novice and beginner. The plain sit-up has the same conflict, so it is a library-level issue and not something to fix here.

name: Sit-Up
sources: Sit-Ups (1-Min, Cooper): Males, Age 20-29 (secondary site citing Cooper Institute 2013 monograph) <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29> ; Police academy fitness chart (Westmoreland) <https://westmoreland.edu/academics/pdfs/police-academy/fitness-charts-curriculum-standards-7.12.23.pdf>
method: Two sources for men 20-29 on the Cooper 1-minute sit-up test. Percentiles mapped: 25th for beginner, 50th for intermediate, about 80th for advanced, 95th for elite. Novice = round(0.67 x beginner). The Cooper 5th percentile of 27 sits near novice.
check: Cooper 1-minute norms for men 20-29: 25th to 30th percentile about 35, 50th = 40, 75th = 46, 95th = 55. Mapping these to beginner 33, intermediate 40, advanced 47 and elite 55 follows the percentile rule closely, and novice 22 matches 0.67 x 33. Both sources trace back to the same Cooper data, so they are not independent, and this is a timed test rather than a single-set max.

name: Spider Crawl
method: No source found. Sit-up / 1.2 from first pass; reps count alternating steps.
check: No source exists. Sit-up/1.2, counting alternating steps, is plausible next to Mountain Climber (12/18/47/75/107). It has no variant links, and its tiers increase. A max-rep test is of limited meaning for a locomotion move, so confidence is low.

name: Spiderman plank
method: No source found. Sit-up / 1.2 from first pass.
check: No source exists. Counting alternating reps, the band is plausible: novice 18 reps is about a 30-40 s plank, close to the novice forearm plank of 37 s, and it sits between the sit-up chain and Mountain Climber. Its easier move (high plank) is a hold. Its harder move, Body Saw (3/5/10/14/22), is lower at every tier, so the order holds.

name: Standing Side Crunches
method: No source found. Easier than sit-up, so sit-up x1.2 ceil (first pass).
check: Current sit-up final 22/33/40/47/55 x1.2 ceil = 27/40/48/57/66; the arithmetic checks, and the band sits above the harder sit-up. StrengthLevel has no data for this move.

name: Straddle L-Sit
sources: Gymnastics Bodies forum: static hold times <https://www.gymnasticbodies.com/forum/topic/3945-static-hold-times>
method: Only a secondhand forum threshold (15 s for straddle) plus L-sit chain from the L-sit anchor 5/10/30/45/60. Searches for confirmation were rate-limited. Kept first pass.
check: The only evidence is a single secondhand forum threshold of 15 s, so it stays derived. The band sits below its easier L-Sit (hf_105, 5/10/30/45/60) and Tuck L-sit (7/10/20/30/45). It sits above the V-Sit (2/5/10/15/25, derived from this band /1.2) and the harder Manna (1/2/4/6/10). Its tiers strictly increase. It is below plain L-sit/1.2 (4/8/25/38/50), which fits the straddle's higher compression demand.

name: Superman Hold
sources: Biering-Sorensen Test (SRAlab, Demoulin 2006) <https://www.sralab.org/rehabilitation-measures/biering-sorensen-test> ; Biering-Sorenson Test (Physio-pedia) <https://www.physio-pedia.com/Biering-Sorenson_Test> ; Mbada 2009 Nigerian reference values (via search summary) <https://e-space.mmu.ac.uk/630024/9/Revised%20Manuscript.pdf>
method: Closest test is the Biering-Sorensen back extensor hold, which is not identical to a floor superman. The values disagree by more than 25% (113 s vs 198 s), so I took the median of about 120 (Mbada all-sample mean 113, men higher), about 137 (Physio-pedia range 80-194 midpoint) and 198 (Demoulin healthy men). That gives intermediate 135 s. Other tiers use the side-plank anchor ratios (x2.25), with novice = round(0.67 x beginner).
check: All three sources give Biering-Sorensen test values (legs supported, arms crossed), not superman-hold values, so the status becomes derived. A floor superman with arms overhead and legs lifted has a longer lever and is harder to hold. I took the researcher's BS median of 135 s, divided it by 1.2 to get 110 s for intermediate, and kept the researcher's side-plank ratios. Novice = 0.67 x 55, rounded to 35. The result is close to the forearm plank anchor and the old placeholder elite of 220, and it removes the impractical 270 s elite.

name: Suspended Fallout
method: No source found. Kept first pass band; checker noted sit-up / 1.2 overstates an anti-extension move.
check: No source exists. The band is plausible: a suspended fallout lets the lifter adjust the angle and is usually easier than a full Ab Wheel Rollout (hf_113, 3/5/10/14/22, sourced), so higher numbers are reasonable. It is well below the sit-up chain, as an anti-extension move should be. It has no variant links. Confidence is low.

name: Suspended Reverse Crunch
sources: Reverse Crunches Strength Standards (StrengthLevel) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/reverse-crunches>
method: Only one usable source (StrengthLevel reverse crunch, lifter-logged, unsuspended, no time window). FitnessVolt's table is explicitly editorial and ratio-derived from the same data, so it is not independent. Kept the graph parent: easier variant of sit-up (22/33/40/47/55) x1.2, ceil.
check: The result is derived, so verification was optional. I opened the StrengthLevel reverse crunch page anyway. It confirms men's Novice 13, Intermediate 32, Advanced 55, Elite 82, average 32. The same site's sit-up page gives 25/54/90/133, average 54, so an unsuspended reverse crunch comes out at about 0.6x sit-up. That is one lifter-logged source, and it is not suspended, so it is not enough to override the graph. The band is kept as sit-up x1.2 to respect harderId=fedb_sit_up. Tiers increase. Plausibility flag: a suspension-strap reverse crunch starts from a plank and is probably harder than a sit-up, so a novice value of 27 looks high. If the product team re-orders the graph, use about 13/20/24/28/33 (sit-up x0.59).

name: Toe Taps
method: No source found for toe taps under any synonym. Kept sit-up x1.2 as a light lying ab move; no better parent available.
check: No sources. The band is sit-up x1.2, which fits a light lying toe-tap move. Tiers increase. No graph neighbours are in this group. Low confidence.

name: Toe Touchers
method: No direct norms found. Kept the graph position between alternate heel touchers and V-up (V-up = sit-up/1.2, so toe touchers = V-up x1.2 = sit-up tiers 22/33/40/47/55).
check: No sources. The band equals the sit-up band (V-up x1.2). Its harderId, hf_120 (V-Up, 18/28/33/39/46), is in this group, and toe touchers come out at or above V-up at every tier, so the order holds. Tiers increase.

name: Toes to bar
sources: Toes to bar strength standards (StrengthLevel) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/toes-to-bar/kg> ; Toes to bar strength standards (FitnessVolt) <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/toes-to-bar/>
method: Two StrengthLevel-style tables for men. StrengthLevel gives novice 5, intermediate 15, advanced 28, elite 42. FitnessVolt (180 lb male) gives 6/16/29/43. They agree within about 6% at intermediate, so I averaged them, using StrengthLevel novice as Aurora beginner and rounding halves up. Aurora novice = round(0.67 x 6).
check: The StrengthLevel and FitnessVolt tables are kipping-friendly CrossFit user data, and FitnessVolt likely copies StrengthLevel. Their intermediate of 16 and elite of 43 sit far above the hanging knee raise anchor (3/8/12/15/20), but strict toes-to-bar is a harder hanging-core move. I capped each tier at hanging knee raise divided by 1.2 (3/7/10/13/17) and kept the lower source value where it was smaller (beginner 6).

name: Torso Twist
method: An unloaded standing or seated torso twist is a rotational mobility and warm-up move with no point of failure, so max reps is not meaningful. Agrees with the checker's note.
check: An unloaded torso twist is a mobility and warm-up rotation with no point of failure, so a max-rep band means nothing. Agree with the checker and the researcher.

name: Tuck Crunch
method: No direct norms found. Kept the graph parent: easier variant of sit-up, sit-up x1.2 ceil.
check: No sources. The band is sit-up x1.2 because harderId is fedb_sit_up. Tiers increase. It is plausible next to the crunch anchor (16/24/40/60/85) at the middle tiers.

name: Tuck L-sit
sources: L-Sit Tutorial (Simonster Strength) <https://exercises.kemitchell.com/sources/Simonster-Strength-l-sit-tutorial> ; L-sit exercise guide (FitnessVolt) <https://fitnessvolt.com/l-sit-exercise-guide/>
method: Two weak coaching sources: a Simonster-style tutorial wants a 10 s tuck hold before training, which I mapped to beginner, and FitnessVolt uses a 30 s tuck L-sit as the pass mark, which I mapped to advanced. Intermediate set between them at 20, elite 45, novice = round(0.67 x 10).
check: The numbers are plausible: a 10 s beginner hold and a 30 s advanced hold match common progression gates, and they sit above the straddle L-sit at every tier. The sources are coaching gates rather than population norms, so the status should be derived. The exercises.kemitchell.com URL looks like a mirror or aggregator rather than the original Simonster page and should be treated as unverified. The old placeholder (15/30/60/90/120) was far too high.

name: V-Sit
method: No tiered hold standards found. Kept the straddle L-sit /1.2 derivation. Coaching pages give only a vague 30 s V-sit target (Fatherly, Peloton), with no tiers and no stated method, so they are not used as numbers. Tiers increase.
check: No sourced hold tiers. The band is straddle L-sit /1.2, rounded. Tiers increase and stay below the L-sit anchor (5/10/30/45/60), which is plausible for a harder compression hold. The 30 s figure in general coaching guides is unverified and not used. Its neighbours hf_105 and hf_107 are not in this group. Low confidence.

name: V-Up
method: Only per-set training guidance found (e.g. WebMD tiers by sets of 5-8 / 9-19 / 20+ reps, from a search summary; the page fetch failed), which is not max-rep data and could not be verified, so it is not used. Kept sit-up /1.2.
check: I tried strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/v-ups, and the page has no V-up standards. A web search also found no V-up max-rep norms, only sit-up proxies. The band is kept as sit-up /1.2. It sits below toe touchers, which is in this group, at every tier. Tiers increase. Plausibility flag: novice 18 and beginner 28 are above the crunch anchor (16/24), although a V-up is harder than a crunch. This comes from the upstream sit-up band (22/33 at the low tiers), not from this derivation. Low confidence.

name: Wind Sprints
method: No source for this exercise name. Treated as an alternating knee-pull move at sit-up level. Mountain climbers on StrengthLevel (reported average about 47 for men, community data) look comparable to sit-up levels, which loosely supports this, but it is not a true synonym and the tempo differs.
check: No sources for this name. The band is set equal to sit-up as an alternating knee-pull move. Tiers increase. The move is pace-driven. Low confidence.

name: Windshield Wiper
method: No numbers found for the hanging windshield wiper. The first search matched only car wipers, and later searches were rate limited. Kept the hanging knee raise anchor (3/8/12/15/20) /1.2 as a harder hanging core move.
check: I searched again and found only car-wiper results, with no exercise norms. The band is hanging knee raise /1.2, which is plausible for an advanced hanging rotation move. Tiers increase. Its harderId, hf_106 (V-Sit), is in this group, but that is a hold measured in seconds and this move is counted in reps, so the order check does not apply. Low confidence.

check: Low-load abduction activation drill; not a max test, so no tiers.

name: Copenhagen Adduction Exercise
sources: Physiotutors / physio wiki Copenhagen prescription <https://www.physiotutors.com/?p=9296>
method: Searched for CAE max-rep norms. Found only a max-rep protocol (Prehab Guys, no norms), a 2026 smartphone reliability study (MDPI Sports 14(4):125, page returned 403 so no numbers read) and a 3-maximal-rep load-cell test. No published rep-to-failure norms and no sensible bodyweight-rep parent among the anchors, so no band is proposed.
check: No rep-to-failure norms exist; the only figures are training prescriptions and a 3-rep load-cell protocol. No sensible bodyweight-rep parent. A Copenhagen plank hold would be a better test variant.

check: Loaded lift; max reps depend on the weight chosen, and the published standards are weight-based.

check: Loaded lift; max reps depend on the weight chosen.

name: Dumbbell Single-leg Hip Thrust
sources: Establishing normative values for the single leg bridge endurance test (IJSPT) <https://ijspt.scholasticahq.com/article/154592.pdf>
method: Parent is Unilateral Hip Thrust (itself derived from the single-leg bridge test, 27 +/- 7 reps) at 12/18/23/28/33. Dumbbell-loaded version is harder, so parent / 1.2 rounded up: 10/15/20/24/28. The unloaded single-leg bridge hold norm (65.2 s, SD 32.7, Worst and Henderson 2026) is a time test and was not converted. No direct source for the loaded move; dumbbell weight is unspecified, so treat as an estimate.
check: Taken from the Unilateral Hip Thrust band (12/18/23/28/33) with the harder-variant rule (/1.2, rounded up). Bands strictly increase and sit below the parent at every tier. Low confidence because the dumbbell weight is not specified. This is inconsistent with wger_1736 (dumbbell SLDL), which was marked not_max_test. Reviewers should choose one policy for light-dumbbell moves.

name: Flutter Kicks
sources: Flutter Kicks Strength Standards (Strength Level) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/flutter-kicks>
method: No clinical or military rep norm found. Only one numeric source: Strength Level user-submitted men's table (novice 19, intermediate 51, advanced 93, elite 145). Strength Level tiers are percentile-based (novice ~20th, intermediate ~50th, advanced ~80th, elite ~95th), so mapped to Aurora beginner/intermediate/advanced/elite directly: beginner 19, intermediate 51, advanced 93, elite 145; novice = round(0.67 x 19) = 13. FitnessVolt (14/67/140/228) is an editorial table, not a measured population, so not used as a second source. Single source, so kept derived; counting convention (each kick vs pair) is not stated.
check: Fetched the Strength Level page. Men's figures are confirmed: Beginner <1 (5th pct), Novice 19 (20th), Intermediate 51 (50th), Advanced 93 (80th), Elite 145 (95th). The percentile mapping to Aurora beginner to elite is correct, and novice = round(0.67 x 19) = 13. This is one self-reported user source, so it stays derived. The high elite value relative to crunches (85) fits a low-load move where every kick counts as a rep.

name: Hyperextensions With No Hyperextension Bench
sources: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine 5:656 (dynamic lumbar endurance) <https://www.jssm.org/jssm-05-656.xml-Fulltext>
method: Re-checked. Dynamic back-extension endurance on a BackUP dynamometer: 17.4 +/- 4.9 and 16.6 +/- 3.9 reps, n=16 (8 men, 8 women), JSSM 5:656 (reliability study, no norms; confirmed on the full text). The 2021 Bigham/Osborne dynamic back extension normative paper exists but its numbers were not accessible (abstract only). Only one numeric source, so first-pass band retained: intermediate 17, other tiers scaled with hanging knee raise ratios.
check: New, better-matched source: Alaranta et al. 1994, Scand J Rehabil Med 26:211-215 (open full text at medicaljournalssweden.se/jrm/article/download/41795/47386/121641; I read Tables I-IV). The repetitive arch-up test is this exact move: prone with the hips at the edge of the table, ankles held, trunk raised from 45 degrees of flexion to horizontal, 1 rep per 2-3 s, capped at 50. Table IV gives all men aged 35-39 at 29 +/- 13 reps (n=242 men overall; adjusted male mean 28). Arch-up showed no significant age effect, so it applies to men aged 20-29. Normal-percentile mapping: beginner 29-0.84x13=18, intermediate 29, advanced 40, elite 29+1.64x13=50 (also the test cap), novice round(0.67x18)=12. This replaces the earlier 4/11/17/21/28 band, which came from a resisted BackUP dynamometer (JSSM 5:656) and is a different device. The new band sits plausibly just below the crunches anchor, matching Alaranta's own sit-up figure (27) being close to arch-up (28). One population source, so it stays derived.

sources: Horizontal Pull-Up Test (TopEndSports) <https://www.topendsports.com/testing/tests/pull-up-horizontal.htm> ; Modified Pull-Up Test (TopEndSports, FITNESSGRAM protocol) <https://www.topendsports.com/testing/tests/pull-up-modified.htm>

The straight-leg inverted row is the harder variant, so /1.2 gives beginner 10, intermediate 14, advanced 20, elite 25. (2) The FITNESSGRAM / TopEndSports modified pull-up, done straight-bodied with weight on the heels (a straight-leg inverted row to a low bar): 'Adults typically aim for 10-15 repetitions', midpoint 12.5, and the boys' norms reach 14 at age 17. Intermediate is the average of 14 and 12.5, which gives 13 (the two agree within 25%). Other tiers come from source 1 /1.2. Novice = round(0.67 x 10) = 7.

The modified pull-up page (straight body, weight on heels, which is a true inverted-row synonym) confirms 'Adults typically aim for 10-15 repetitions' and boys 14 reps at age 17, but this is guidance or a HFZ threshold, not a percentile table. The bent-knee horizontal pull-up page confirms its table, but that is an easier variant, not a synonym. That gives only 1 confirmed source for this exercise, so it is downgraded to derived. The best trusted neighbour is the measured bent-knee table: midpoints 12/17/24.5/30 /1.2 = 10/14/20/25, with intermediate blended with the 12.5 guidance to 13 and novice = round(0.67x10) = 7, which gives 7/10/13/20/25. Against the current neighbour 3/4/8/13/18 the constraint fails at every tier because of the confirmed misfire; re-band the neighbour. Tiers strictly increase.
